'''Johannes Jisse (Hans) Duistermaat''' ([[The Hague]], December 20, 1942 – [[Utrecht]], March 19, 2010) was a Dutch mathematician.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hans Duistermaat |url=https://gqt.nl/for-researchers/members/hans-duistermaat/ |access-date=2022-08-18 |website=Geometry and Quantum Theory (GQT) |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=In memoriam: Prof. dr. Johannes Jisse Duistermaat |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Duistermaat_Johannes_Jisse/CV |access-date=2022-08-16 |website=[[Academia Europaea]]}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Duistermaat attended primary school in [[Jakarta]], at the time the capital of the [[Dutch East Indies]], where his family moved after the end of [[World War II]]. In 1957, a few years after the [[Dutch–Indonesian Round Table Conference|Indonesian independence]], they came back to the Netherlands and Duistermaat completed his high school studies in [[Vlaardingen]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=de Waard |first=Peter |date=2010-04-12 |title=De man van de formule |language=nl |trans-title=The man of the formula |work=[[De Volkskrant]] |url=https://webspace.science.uu.nl/~kolk0101/Duistermaat%20IM/DuisVOLKS.jpg}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite news |last=Kreulen |first=Edwin |date=2010-04-19 |title=De wiskunde bleef altijd roepen. Hans Duistermaat 1942-2010 |language=nl |trans-title=Mathematics always keeps calling. Hans Duistermaat 1942-2010 |pages=25 |work=[[Trouw]] |url=https://webspace.science.uu.nl/~kolk0101/Duistermaat%20IM/DuisTROUW.pdf}}</ref>

From 1959 to 1965 he studied mathematics at [[Utrecht University]], and he obtained his PhD degree at the same institution in 1968, with a thesis on the mathematical structures of [[thermodynamics]] entitled "''Energy and Entropy as Real Morphisms for Addition and Order''".<ref name=":0">{{MathGenealogy|id=45240|name=Johannes Jisse Duistermaat}}</ref> His original supervisor was the applied mathematician Günther K. Braun, who died one year before the thesis defense, so the official supervision was taken over by geometer [[Hans Freudenthal]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=van den Ban |first1=Erik |last2=Kolk |first2=Johan |date=2010 |title=In Memoriam Hans Duistermaat (1942-2010): Grasping the essence |url=http://www.nieuwarchief.nl/serie5/pdf/naw5-2010-11-4-235.pdf |journal=Nieuw Archief voor Wiskunde |volume=11 |issue=5 |pages=235–237}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite arXiv |eprint=1110.5627 |class=math.HO |first=Reyer |last=Sjamaar |title=Hans Duistermaat's contributions to Poisson geometry |date=2011-10-25}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |date=2011 |editor-last=Guillemin |editor-first=Victor |editor-link=Victor Guillemin |editor2-last=Pelayo |editor2-first=Álvaro |editor3-last=Vũ Ngọc |editor3-first=San |editor4-last=Weinstein |editor4-first=Alan |editor4-link=Alan Weinstein |title=Remembering Johannes J. Duistermaat (1942–2010) |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201106/201106FullIssue.pdf |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=58 |issue=6 |pages=794–802}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite journal |last=Cushman |first=Richard |date=2011 |title=Hans Duistermaat (1942-2010) |url=https://www.ems-ph.org/journals/newsletter/pdf/2011-03-79.pdf |journal=Newsletter of the European Mathematical Society |publisher=[[European Mathematical Society]] |volume=79 |pages=17–19}}</ref>

After a postdoctoral stay in [[Lund University|Lund]] (1969–70), Duistermaat returned to the Netherlands in 1971 and became in 1972 full professor in [[Radboud University Nijmegen|Nijmegen]]. In 1974 he returned to Utrecht, where he was offered the chair of Freudenthal.

In 2004 he was awarded a special [[Academy professor|academy professorship]] by the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences|KNAW]], allowing him to focus exclusively on research, even after his official retirement in 2007.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=van der Vorst |first=H.A. |date=2011 |title=Levensbericht Johannes Jisse Duistermaat |trans-title=Life story of Johannes Jisse Duistermaat |url=https://dwc.knaw.nl/DL/levensberichten/PE00009241.pdf |journal=Jaarboek - Koninklijke Nederlandse Akademie van Wetenschappen |publisher=[[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]]}}</ref><ref name=":4" /> He died in March 2010, due to [[non-Hodgkin lymphoma]] and [[pneumonia]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Overlijden Hans Duistermaat |trans-title=Death of Hans Duistermaat |url=https://www.math.uu.nl/news/overlijden-hans.duistermaat.html |access-date=2022-08-16 |website=[[Utrecht University]] |language=nl}}</ref>

He was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1982,<ref>{{cite web |author= |date= |title=J.J. Duistermaat (1942 - 2010) |url=http://www.dwc.knaw.nl/biografie/pmknaw/?pagetype=authorDetail&aId=PE00009241 |accessdate=14 July 2015 |publisher=[[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] |language=Dutch}}</ref> and of [[Academia Europaea]] in 1993.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Johannes Jisse Duistermaat |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Duistermaat_Johannes_Jisse |access-date=2022-08-16 |website=[[Academia Europaea]]}}</ref> In 2007 he became a Knight of the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2007-04-27 |title=Lintjesregen: De opvallendste feiten op een rij |language=nl |trans-title=Annual award celebration: the most notable facts in a row |work=[[RTV Utrecht]] |url=https://www.rtvutrecht.nl/nieuws/151747/lintjesregen-de-opvallendste-feiten-op-een-rij}}</ref><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite journal |last=Vũ Ngọc |first=San |date=2011 |title=Johannes Jisse (dit Hans) Duistermaat (1942-2010) |url=https://webspace.science.uu.nl/~kolk0101/Duistermaat%20IM/DuisSAN.pdf |journal=La Gazette des mathématiciens |language=fr |publisher=[[Société mathématique de France]] |volume=127 |pages=84–91}}</ref>

Apart from being an eminent mathematician, Duistermaat was also a [[chess]] player. In a simultaneous match of 10 against [[Anatoly Karpov]] in 1977, Duistermaat was the only one who did not lose.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Beekman |first=Robert |date=2016 |title=Simultaan Karpov (1977) |trans-title=Simultaneous Karpov (1977) |url=http://oudzuylenutrecht.nl/simultaan-karpov-1977/ |access-date=2022-08-16 |website=Schaakclub Oud Zuylen Utrecht |language=nl}}</ref>

== Research ==
Duistermaat defined himself a [[Geometric analysis|geometric analyst]],<ref name=":2" /> but his research covered many different areas in [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]], [[geometry]] and [[mathematical physics]], including [[classical mechanics]], [[symplectic geometry]], [[Fourier integral operator]]s, [[partial differential equations]], [[algebraic geometry]], [[harmonic analysis]], and [[dynamical systems]].

Duistermaat dropped thermodynamics after his PhD, due to dissents between mathematicians and physicists in Utrecht. Nevertheless, during his PhD research he read the work by [[Sophus Lie]], and in particular encountered [[Contact Transformation|contact transformations]]. These topics exerted an important influence for his future pioneering works in [[microlocal analysis]],<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> most prominently during his collaboration with [[Lars Hörmander]], when they developed the theory of [[Fourier integral operator]]s and proved the [[Propagation of singularities theorem]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duistermaat |first1=J. J. |last2=Hörmander |first2=L. |author-link2=Lars Hörmander |date=1972 |title=Fourier integral operators. II |journal=[[Acta Mathematica]] |volume=128 |issue=none |pages=183–269 |doi=10.1007/BF02392165 |issn=0001-5962 |doi-access=free |s2cid=189785151}}</ref> This led him also to the work with [[Victor Guillemin]] on the link between spectra of [[Elliptic operator|elliptic operators]] and periodic bicharacteristics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duistermaat |first1=J. J. |last2=Guillemin |first2=V. W. |author-link2=Victor Guillemin |date=1975-02-01 |title=The spectrum of positive elliptic operators and periodic bicharacteristics |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |language=en |volume=29 |issue=1 |pages=39–79 |bibcode=1975InMat..29...39D |doi=10.1007/BF01405172 |issn=1432-1297 |doi-access= |s2cid=189832135}}</ref>

Duistermaat introduced the notion of monodromy in [[Hamiltonian system|Hamiltonian systems]]<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":5" /> as obstruction to the existence of global [[action-angle coordinates]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Duistermaat |first=J. J. |date=1980 |title=On global action-angle coordinates |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cpa.3160330602 |journal=Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics |language=en |volume=33 |issue=6 |pages=687–706 |doi=10.1002/cpa.3160330602|url-access=subscription }}</ref> later, together with Richard Cushman, he extended it to the [[quantum systems]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cushman |first1=R. |last2=Duistermaat |first2=J. J. |date=1988 |title=The quantum mechanical spherical pendulum |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=19 |issue=2 |pages=475–479 |doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1988-15705-9 |doi-access=free |issn=0273-0979}}</ref>

In symplectic geometry he is well known<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":5" /> for his article with his PhD student {{Interlanguage link|Gert Heckman|lt=Gert Heckman|de}} on the [[Duistermaat–Heckman formula]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duistermaat |first1=J. J. |last2=Heckman |first2=G. J. |author-link2= |date=1982-06-01 |title=On the variation in the cohomology of the symplectic form of the reduced phase space |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |language=en |volume=69 |issue=2 |pages=259–268 |bibcode=1982InMat..69..259D |doi=10.1007/BF01399506 |issn=1432-1297 |doi-access= |s2cid=119943006}}</ref> which will later be placed in the more general framework of [[equivariant cohomology]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Heckman |first=Gert |author-link= |date=2010 |title=In Memoriam Hans Duistermaat (1942-2010): Recollections of a godsend talent |url=http://www.nieuwarchief.nl/serie5/pdf/naw5-2010-11-4-240.pdf |journal=Nieuw Archief voor Wiskunde |volume=11 |issue=5 |pages=240–241}}</ref> independently by [[Nicole Berline|Berline]] and [[Michèle Vergne|Vergne]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Berline |first1=Nicole |author-link=Nicole Berline |last2=Vergne |first2=Michèle |author-link2=Michèle Vergne |date=1982 |title=Classes caracteristiques equivariantes. Formule de localisation en cohomologie equivariante |trans-title=Equivariant characteristic classes. Localisation formula in equivariant cohomology |url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k62356694/f77.item |journal=Comptes rendus de l'Académie des sciences |language=fr |volume=295 |pages=539–541}}</ref> and by [[Michael Atiyah|Atiyah]] and [[Raoul Bott|Bott]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Atiyah |first1=M.F. |last2=Bott |first2=R. |date=1984 |title=The moment map and equivariant cohomology |journal=[[Topology (journal)|Topology]] |language=en |volume=23 |issue=1 |pages=1–28 |doi=10.1016/0040-9383(84)90021-1 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Other contributions in this field include a generalisation of the Morse index theorem<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Duistermaat |first=J. J |date=1976-08-01 |title=On the Morse index in variational calculus |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |language=en |volume=21 |issue=2 |pages=173–195 |doi=10.1016/0001-8708(76)90074-8 |doi-access=free |issn=0001-8708}}</ref> and a contribution to the problem of [[Quantization commutes with reduction|quantisation commutes with reduction]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duistermaat |first1=Hans |last2=Guillemin |first2=Victor |author-link2=Victor Guillemin |last3=Meinrenken |first3=Eckhard |author-link3=Eckhard Meinrenken |last4=Wu |first4=Siye |date=1995 |title=Symplectic reduction and Riemann-Roch for circle actions |journal=Mathematical Research Letters |language=en |volume=2 |issue=3 |pages=259–266 |doi=10.4310/MRL.1995.v2.n3.a3 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

In his book on [[Lie group|Lie groups]], together with his PhD student Johan Kolk,<ref>{{Cite book |last1=J. J. |first1=Duistermaat |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-642-56936-4 |title=Lie Groups |last2=Kolk |first2=J. A. C. |publisher=[[Springer Verlag]] |year=2000 |isbn=978-3-540-15293-4 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-56936-4}}</ref> he provided an alternative proof of the [[Lie's third theorem|third Lie theorem]], which will turn out to be crucial for proving the analogous theorem for [[Lie groupoid|Lie groupoids]] and for its applications to [[Poisson geometry]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":5" />

His work with Alberto Grünbaum on the bispectral problem<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duistermaat |first1=J. J. |last2=Grünbaum |first2=F. A. |date=1986-06-01 |title=Differential equations in the spectral parameter |journal=[[Communications in Mathematical Physics]] |language=en |volume=103 |issue=2 |pages=177–240 |bibcode=1986CMaPh.103..177D |doi=10.1007/BF01206937 |doi-access=free |issn=1432-0916 |s2cid=121915958}}</ref> was influential for integrable systems and noncommutative algebraic geometry.<ref name=":5" /> In the last stages of his life he became interested in algebraic geometry<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":7" /> and wrote a book on QRT maps and [[Elliptic surface|elliptic surfaces]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Duistermaat |first=J. J. |title=Discrete integrable systems : QRT Maps and Elliptic Surfaces |date=2010 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-0-387-72923-7 |location=New York |oclc=676697713}}</ref>

Duistermaat contributed also to [[applied mathematics]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> He was a consultant to [[Royal Dutch-Shell|Royal Dutch Shell]], which led to the thesis of Christiaan Stolk on the [[Seismic inversion|inversion of seismic data]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Stolk |first=Christiaan |url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/39700274.pdf |title=On the Modeling and Inversion of Seismic Data |publisher=[[Universiteit Utrecht]] |year=2000 |isbn=90-393-2551-0 |edition= |location=Utrecht |type=PhD thesis}}</ref> He also worked on [[Barrier function|barrier functions]] in [[convex programming]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Duistermaat |first=Hans |date=2001 |title=The universal barrier function of a convex polytope |journal=Circumspice. Various Papers in Around Mathematics in Honour of Arnoud van Rooij |publisher=[[Katholieke Universiteit Nijmegen]] |pages=207–220}}</ref> collaborated with biomedical technologists on [[computer vision]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Loog |first1=Marco |last2=Duistermaat |first2=Johannes |last3=Florack |first3=Luc M. J. |date=2001 |editor-last=Kerckhove |editor-first=Michael |title=On the Behavior of Spatial Critical Points under Gaussian Blurring A Folklore Theorem and Scale-Space Constraints |url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/3-540-47778-0_15 |journal=Scale-Space and Morphology in Computer Vision |language=en |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |pages=183–192 |doi=10.1007/3-540-47778-0_15 |isbn=978-3-540-47778-5|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and with [[Geophysics|geophysicists]] on modeling the [[Polarity reversal|polarity reversals]] of the [[Earth's magnetic field]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hoyng |first1=P. |last2=Duistermaat |first2=J. J. |date=2004-10-01 |title=Geomagnetic reversals and the stochastic exit problem |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/epl/i2004-10243-1/meta |journal=[[Europhysics Letters]] |language=en |volume=68 |issue=2 |pages=177 |doi=10.1209/epl/i2004-10243-1 |bibcode=2004EL.....68..177H |s2cid=250865891 |issn=0295-5075|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

He supervised 25 PhD students.<ref name=":0" />
